transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Tom Blake (SilverLake CTO), Maria Chen (Product), Omar Hassan (Security), Leah Ortiz (ML)

Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on the Model Catalog and choosing open models for a POC. Discussed benchmarks, compatibility matrix (quantization, GPU families), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and private deployment constraints (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed on follow-ups: share benchmark spreadsheet, run a perf estimate for 2k context, schedule deep technical session.

Topics: Model catalog UI, API examples, Redwood Console model filters, Optimize suggestions, benchmark comparators, dedicated vs hosted routing, VPC/private deploy considerations.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros, then we'll jump into the model catalog and i can show how to pick an open model, look at perf numbers and then priya will cover compatibility details.
[00:18] Tom: great, we are excited. we are evaluating open models to reduce cost and want to validate latency for our clinical triage workflow. goal is sub-200ms p50 on chat completions if possible but we know, uh, 2k context might push that.
[00:34] Maria: also interested in how Redwood's Optimize tools help us pick quantization and batching settings, because cost is a big constraint.
[00:44] Priya: awesome, i'll make sure to show the quantization flags and the compatibility matrix — which GPUs are supported for int8, nf4, etc.

[01:10] Alex: opening the model catalog — here you can filter by task, seq len, and verified benchmarks. for example, you can search for open-chat models, then we surface verified latency and tokens/sec on our reference hardware. note that those numbers are on xGXe-80 GPUs, the matrix shows which models have optimized kernels.
[01:45] Tom: when you say "verified benchmarks", are those public tests or internal? do you share the raw load-test results?
[01:52] Alex: good q — we provide a benchmark spreadsheet with test harness config and raw numbers. we also show standard deviation and median p50/p95. we can share the sheet after.

[02:20] Priya: jumping in — compatibility matrix is key. some smaller LLMs have fused kernels and run much faster on Ampere vs Hopper, and quantization support is model-specific. we call out model architecture and whether we recommend int8, nf4 or int4 with caveats. sometimes tokenization differences change latency.
[02:45] Leah: do you have a quick example for 2k context? our triage prompts average 1.8k tokens with a ~300 token reply.
[02:53] Priya: yes — so on a 2k context, KV cache memory increases and attention cost grows quadratically, so batching becomes trickier. for 2k we recommend dedicated pools or optimized kernels with sharding. i'll run a perf estimate for your exact profile.

[03:30] Omar: security question — for private deployments we need KMS/HSM, SOC2, and audit logs; any surprises?
[03:38] Alex: we support customer-managed KMS in Private, SOC2 Type II, and you can push logs to your SIEM. we'll attach the security packet. some on-prem installs require extra network setup but we have templates.

[04:05] Alex: showing API demo — simple REST call example, stream vs non-stream, and how model aliasing works in the catalog. you can pin a model version for a route, and our routing policy can fallback to a cheaper variant.
[04:40] Maria: can we do canary rollouts between an open model and a closed model if we want to compare quality?
[04:46] Priya: yes — console supports canary/A-B and auto rollback if error rates increase. also you can tie evals to prompt sets to detect regressions.

[05:20] Alex: now Optimize — we show suggested batching and cache rules per route. for your workload Optimize might suggest prefix caching for common patient-intake prompts and batching threshold of ~12 requests to hit the sweet spot between latency and tokens/sec.
[05:42] Tom: is that automatic or advisory? we don't want opaque changes that could break latency SLOs.
[05:48] Alex: purely advisory unless you enable auto-tuning. default is suggest-only; you can run in staging to evaluate changes.

[06:10] Priya: technical deep dive note: quantization compatibility table — this shows recommended quantization (int8/nf4) and expected perf impacts. for example, Model-A with nf4 sees ~1.8x throughput improvement on Ampere, with minor quality delta. Model-B recommends int8 and benefits more on newer GPUs.
[06:45] Leah: how do you validate quality regressions from quantized models? do you provide evals?
[06:52] Priya: we integrate eval suites — you give a prompt set and we compute metric deltas and sample outputs so you can review. we also flag hallucination changes.

[07:20] [demo pauses briefly while Alex pulls up benchmark spreadsheet link]
[07:35] Alex: sharing link in chat: benchmark-spreadsheet.redwood/silverlake-demo (note: placeholder). the sheet compares p50/p95, tokens/sec, mem footprint, and recommended GPU families.

[08:05] Maria: for SLA planning, what's typical for hosted vs dedicated? how predictable are these p50 numbers in production?
[08:13] Alex: hosted is best-effort with soft SLOs; dedicated gives predictable throughput and we provide latency targets based on committed capacity. production numbers vary with request mix; that's why we recommend a short smoke test and a pilot.

[09:00] Tom: and fallback behaviors if capacity hits limits? we need graceful degradation not hard failures.
[09:06] Priya: Redwood supports smart routing - fall back to a compatible variant (e.g., smaller quantized model) and you can configure route policies by latency or cost. also burst capacity options exist for Dedicated.

[10:00] Omar: on network — for Private we need to allow only specific CIDRs + private peering, is there a typical template?
[10:07] Alex: yes we have VPC peering and peering templates; some customers put control plane in our hosted control plane while data plane stays private. we'll send the network template.

[11:00] Alex: quick live demo picking a model: filter by "chat, verified benchmark, <=200ms p50" — results show Model-A-int8 and Model-C-nf4. clicking into Model-A shows tokens/sec, mem, and recommended kernel (fused attention).
[11:35] Maria: is the "verified" label based on our workload or Redwood's standard harness?
[11:40] Alex: Redwood standard harness; we recommend you run the harness against your prompts, which we can help with during the POC.

[12:15] Priya: compatibility caveat — some open models have differences in tokenization leading to output length variance; that affects cost estimates. we include tokenization delta in the compatibility matrix.

[13:00] [15–40 minute technical exchange condensed — customer asks about benchmarking reproducibility and sample configs]
[13:10] Priya: i'll attach the exact docker-compose and runner config used for the benchmarks. if you want to reproduce we can also provide a small harness to run against your private data (in your VPC) for accuracy.

[14:00] Tom: our timeline — want to pick model and run a POC in next 6 weeks, then evaluate dedicated reservation. success metrics are: cost per 1k tokens vs baseline, p50 latency under 250ms, and <3% quality regressions vs our current model.
[14:20] Alex: noted. we'll aim to support a rapid POC: share catalog + benchmarks, run perf estimate, then do a 2-week smoke pilot with 1 GPU node in Dedicated or Private.

[15:00] Maria: about pricing — is there a delta for open models vs curated Redwood models?
[15:06] Alex: yes open models typically have lower per-token charges but may require Dedicated for consistency; we price based on model family and compute. i'll include example TCO scenarios in the follow-up.

[16:00] Omar: security follow-ups — we'll need the SOC2 report, IAM patterns (SSO/SAML), and where audit logs are stored.
[16:08] Alex: we'll attach SOC2 and a list of available audit exports and retention options. for SSO we support SAML and OIDC; RBAC in Console.

[16:40] Leah: small question — do you support on-the-fly quantization or do we need to recompile per model?
[16:46] Priya: quantization is typically an offline step for production; Optimize can recommend profiles and in some hosted cases we have pre-quantized variants. for Private we provide tooling for you to run quantization in your environment.

[17:20] Alex: wrapping up demo — recap: we'll send benchmark sheet, compatibility matrix, network template, and security packet. priya will run perf estimate for the 2k context and share numbers. schedule deep dive the following week.

[17:48] Tom: sounds good. one last thing — do you do A/B quality evals against closed models? we'd like to compare against our incumbent vendor.
[17:55] Priya: yes we can run side-by-side evals; you supply the prompt set and we'll produce metric diffs and sample outputs. note that some vendor APIs return slightly different tokenization, so we normalize when possible.

[18:20] Alex: any immediate blockers?
[18:22] Omar: just internal procurement timeline — may need to loop in legal for the NDA but otherwise fine.

[18:40] Maria: ok let's target receiving the follow-ups by next Friday so we can plan the POC start on 2026-04-13.

[19:00] Alex: great, i'll follow up with an email including links and next steps. thanks everyone.

[19:15] Meeting end: quick recap and explicit next steps read out.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few proper noun errors (some model names munged), and there were a couple of overlaps/crosstalk lines especially when multiple customer folks chimed in.

References / Links mentioned: benchmark-spreadsheet.redwood/silverlake-demo (placeholder), security-packet.redwood/silverlake (placeholder), network-template.vpc.redwood (placeholder).
